description: WaterML 2 is the Open Geospatial Consortium's family of standards for exchanging water observation data between information systems. Part 1 (Timeseries, version 2.0.1, OGC 10-126r4) is an information model and XML encoding for hydrological time series built on the Observations and Measurements model and implemented as a Geography Markup Language application schema; Part 2 covers ratings, gaugings and sections (15-018r2); Part 3 is the HY_Features conceptual model of surface hydrology features (14-111r6); Part 4 is GroundWaterML 2 (16-032r2, version 2.2); a best practice profile, WaterML-WQ (14-003), covers water quality, and the earlier CUAHSI WaterML 0.3.0 is kept as a discussion paper. OGC and the World Meteorological Organization developed them through a joint Hydrology Domain Working Group to end the lack of standard formats that hindered re-use of flood forecasting, reporting and water infrastructure data; WaterML 2.0 became an OGC standard in 2012. The documents and schemas are free to download from the OGC page and free to implement. The standards are global and have no temporal coverage of their own. Caveats: they describe how to encode data, not the data themselves, and uptake varies between national hydrological services. Simulation uses: interoperable input of gauge, rating and groundwater series into flood, reservoir and water-supply models and digital twins, and calibration of network-flow models.
